questions.question: During a CDL vehicle inspection test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Replace a tire.
Remove the alternator belt.
Replace spark plugs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: The CDL vehicle inspection test includes checking the engine oil level.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign of drowsy driving?

options.text: Eyes going out of focus by themselves
Having trouble keeping your head up
Drifting from lane to lane
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsy driving include eyes closing or going out of focus, trouble keeping your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you must:

options.text: Keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
Turn to face the road before you finish exiting.
Face away from the vehicle.
Face toward the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face toward the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure.

questions.question: When driving, hold the steering wheel:

options.text: With one hand.
With both hands on opposite sides.
With both hands at the bottom.
With both hands at the top.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands placed on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during a vehicle inspection:

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at slower speeds.
The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is intact.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service until it is repaired.
questions.explanation: Missing or broken leaves in a leaf spring are dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: You must be able to stop your vehicle within:

options.text: 10 feet.
1,000 feet.
The distance you can see ahead on the road.
One minute of braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the area of road you can see. You must slow down whenever visibility decreases.

questions.question: A cargo van with a heavy load is:

options.text: Usually the same height as when it is empty.
Usually taller than when it is lightly loaded.
Usually shorter than when it is lightly loaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually shorter than when it is lightly loaded.
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower than usual. A vehicle is taller when carrying a light load than when carrying a heavy load. If your vehicle fits under an overpass when fully loaded, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS stops working, you should:

options.text: Brake normally.
Pump the brake pedal repeatedly.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible.
Avoid using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents brakes from locking up during hard braking. If ABS fails, your basic brakes still work, so you can continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: A person driving with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A distracted driver.
A person dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.correctAnswerText: A distracted driver.
questions.explanation: Open windows in cold weather can be a sign that a driver is impaired. Drivers who are drowsy, on drugs, have been drinking, or are ill may open windows to stay alert. Watch for this sign in other drivers.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.

options.text: White ice
Black ice
Green ice
Blue ice

questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice that lets the road show through. It looks like the road is just wet.

questions.question: On a bus, where should carry-on baggage be stored?

options.text: In a way that lets riders exit through any window or door in an emergency.
In the aisle near the front of the bus.
On passengers' laps.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a way that lets riders exit through any window or door in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Keep the aisles and stairwells clear. Put luggage in a spot where passengers can exit through any window or door if there is an emergency.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Park in a crowded area near trees.
Pull into a service station.
Park near other vehicles.
Park in an open area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in an open area.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop right away. Park in an open area away from things that could catch fire, like plants or other vehicles. Do not go to a service station.

questions.question: What should you know about railroad crossings?

options.text: You will hear every train that is approaching.
You may not hear a train, even if one is coming.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is coming.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear an approaching train. The train operator may not sound the horn, or it may be prohibited in that area. Even if the horn sounds, noise in your vehicle may keep you from hearing it until the train is too close.

questions.question: In cold weather, when do bridges usually freeze?

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Drive slowly and carefully on bridges and overpasses when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: What do slippery roadways usually do?

options.text: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to drive a vehicle.
Can be avoided by driving at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Be careful when driving on surfaces that could be slippery.

questions.question: What is true about gasoline on a bus?

options.text: It can be brought onto a bus.
It may never be brought onto a bus.
It can be stored in the passenger area during long trips.
It should be stored in glass containers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may never be brought onto a bus.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers and passengers cannot bring hazardous items like gasoline or car batteries onto a bus.

questions.question: Is it okay to fuel a bus while passengers are on board?

options.text: Only at night.
Only on trips longer than 100 miles.
Only if it cannot be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if it cannot be avoided.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus with passengers on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with riders inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: How can you tell if a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: There is a sticker on the control panel.
There is a yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
The letters "ABS" are on the brake pedal.
There is a metal plate on the driver's side door.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will have a yellow ABS warning lamp on the instrument panel.

questions.question: Which person should motorists NOT worry about as a distracted person?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people not paying attention to the road. Watch out for drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and road workers.

questions.question: What should you do when making tight maneuvers?

options.text: Open your door for a better view.
Use your mirrors.
Flash your headlights.
Open the cargo door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This is especially important when driving in tight spaces.
